text: dsh-swarm-orchestrator 是面向 DSH Web 的多 agent 编排插件：它通过 swarm_dispatch 接收任务 DAG，由架构师、构建者、审查者和集成人员等角色并行推进工作，并提供模型选择与回退、任务证据检查、审查反馈循环和失败重试。用户可在 Swarm 网页面板查看看板、流程图、运行状态并配置角色；也可用 /swarm 命令发起目标或处理等待人工决策的任务。适合希望把较大目标拆成可追踪并行工作的 DSH 用户。插件运行在 DSH Web host 中，使用本地存储；不要求额外 API key。

dsh-swarm-orchestrator coordinates DSH agents on parallel task DAGs with role-based models, review loops, retries, and evidence checks. Its web dashboard shows runs and task flow; /swarm starts goals and handles human decisions. Runs in DSH Web with local storage and no extra API key.

dsh-swarm-orchestrator 的功能「任务图派发」：将目标提交为带角色、依赖关系和审查要求的任务图，独立任务可并行运行。
dsh-swarm-orchestrator 的功能「按角色执行与模型选择」：为任务指定角色和模型，执行器依据角色配置生成任务 agent 提示并推进工作。
dsh-swarm-orchestrator 的功能「审查与反馈循环」：已完成任务可交由指定审查角色判断；审查拒绝时附反馈进入后续修订。
dsh-swarm-orchestrator 的功能「任务证据约束」：任务可声明文件、命令或结构化产物证据，并按运行策略决定校验要求。
dsh-swarm-orchestrator 的功能「看板与流程图」：Swarm 页面在 Board、Flow 和 Roster 视图中呈现运行任务、依赖流程和角色配置。
dsh-swarm-orchestrator 的功能「斜杠命令控制」：用户可用 /swarm 发起目标、查询状态、重试任务或提交完成决策。

Role-based AI swarms for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness). Give it a goal, get a team: an architect breaks the work into a task graph, parallel builders execute it, reviewers hold the line, and an integrator ships the result — while you watch the whole thing move on a live kanban board.

dsh-swarm-orchestrator README · dsh-swarm-orchestrator：It runs **inside** your `dsh web` host. No daemon, no second process, no glue scripts. Task agents are ordinary DSH subagents with your tool access and your models; the orchestrator is just a well-behaved Cordis plugin.

dsh-swarm-orchestrator README · dsh-swarm-orchestrator：It has already shipped real work: the first production run reverse-engineered a biotech research dashboard and rebuilt it as a **six-indication suite** (680 curated clinical trials across six cancers) in a single afternoon — five data-curation agents working in parallel, every deliverable machine-verified.

dsh-swarm-orchestrator README · Why not just ask one agent?：Because one agent serializes. Long research tasks queue behind quick edits, context fills up, quality drifts, and nothing checks the output but the same model that wrote it.

This plugin takes the coordination seriously so you don't have to:
section: Why not just ask one agent?

text:
dsh-swarm-orchestrator README · Why not just ask one agent?：- **Parallel by construction.** Tasks declare dependencies (`blockedBy`); everything independent runs at once, bounded by a concurrency cap that adapts when the provider struggles.
- **Every role gets its own model.** Pin DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi, Claude — any model configured in DSH — to any role, with an ordered fallback chain and a per-role reasoning-effort ladder. The picker reads your live model catalog, so new providers show up automatically.
- **Review before "done" means done.** Tasks tagged `reviewBy` are judged by a reviewer agent against the task brief; a rejection loops back to the builder with the feedback attached. Want the last word yourself? Set `reviewGate: "human"` and approve from the dashboard.
- **Failure is a state, not a mystery.** Provider timeouts, quota exhaustion, bad evidence — each is detected, reported plainly, and handled: retries with resume hints, run pause/resume instead of burn-down, automatic model rotation after repeated failures.
- **Scoped to where you are.** Each chat's Swarm tab shows the runs for that chat's workspace; a persisted switch reveals everything on the machine when you want t

text: dsh-swarm-orchestrator README · Why not just ask one agent?：> ⚠️ **Running multiple swarms from different workspaces in parallel**: this is supported and safe with the global cap. However, be mindful that each swarm agent is an in-process session on the host. We recommend **max 2 concurrent runs** unless your host has headroom for more - the global cap defaults to 100 in-process agents, which suits a large machine. If you experience `ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED` (host crash), lower `maxTotalConcurrentAgents` in the Runtime settings.

text: dsh-swarm-orchestrator README · Reviewed hardening plan (0.6.33)：This release implements the reviewed S0–S7 hardening plan. A rebuilt bundle or build receipt is not proof that an already-running host loaded it: deployment needs an intentional reload/restart and an exclusive-storage upgrade check.

dsh-swarm-orchestrator README · Reviewed hardening plan (0.6.33)：- **Physical ownership survives cancellation.** Same-task replacement, dependent readers, reviews and recovery wait for retained child/Shell holders to drain, even with spare capacity. Persisted reviews resume the same attempt once; builder success and acceptance-pending are committed together. A run cannot announce completion while its writers drain.
- **Execution is not acceptance.** New runs persist policy version 1 and separate execution, artifact, acceptance and provenance states. Legacy policy-absent histories keep their historical advisory/fail-open meaning. Task overrides can strengthen, never weaken, the run policy.
- **Evidence:** `advisory` (default) records file/structural warnings; `required` holds missing/invalid artifacts. Commands always require zero exit. Artifact contracts validate bounded regular files, JSON/JSONL/text/binary shape, own required keys, optional schema version, record count and SHA-256. Readable invalid bytes still have content identity. This is structural validation, not scientific/clinical approval or immutable publication.
- **Review:** `warn` (default) labels unavailable/exhausted

dsh-swarm-orchestrator README · Storage upgrade and operational recovery：A writable `EventStore` acquires a non-expiring exclusive-create `.owner` marker **before loading or torn-tail repair** and holds it through append/fsync/rollback and service drain. A second cooperating writer refuses to open; it never silently becomes a reader. `new EventStore(file, { readOnly: true })` is an explicit write-free replay snapshot, not a concurrent transaction or automatic tail repair.

dsh-swarm-orchestrator README · Storage upgrade and operational recovery：New appends use **store protocol 3**, so older readers refuse rather than silently ignore acceptance/budget semantics. Existing legacy/v2 records and original stored cursors are preserved, not rewritten. Back up quiescent storage before a deliberate upgrade; **do not downgrade a protocol-3 store to an older binary**. A crash leaves its marker: only an operator who has proved **all** old writers stopped may preserve the marker as incident evidence and perform manual recovery. PID age, heartbeat expiry and epochs are not permission to steal it. This coordinates cooperating local writers on an atomic-exclusive-create filesystem; it does not fence raw writers, marker deletion, namespace replacement or remote/distributed filesystems, nor promise directory-entry durability after power loss.

dsh-swarm-orchestrator README · Safe validation and deployment gate：Default `npm test` uses an owned temporary `DSH_HOME` and excludes the two deployment suites. Opt-in suites require `DSH_SWARM_LIVE_TESTS=1` **and** explicit exported fixtures (`DSH_SWARM_LIVE_STORAGE`, `DSH_SWARM_LIVE_SETTINGS`); they do not fall back to operator storage. No active production session/log is a test fixture.

dsh-swarm-orchestrator README · Safe validation and deployment gate：`npm run build` emits a full SHA-256 input/output receipt in `lib/build-receipt.json`; the freshness test checks source bytes, generated outputs and toolchain, including restored-mtime edits. `npm run verify:build` also verifies the full receipt, compiled public exports and native tool registration without applying a Host or invoking tools. A standalone client build is explicitly client-only and cannot certify the host build. The next release/deployment still requires its own authorization, isolated upgrade/restart checks and confirmation of the loaded host/client revision. S8 research-pilot reruns, expansion and clinical acceptance remain separately gated.

dsh-swarm-orchestrator README · Notices reach the running chat (0.6.32)：Swarm notices — the run result and the "waiting on a human" attention ping — now reach the dispatching chat *while its turn is still running*, instead of sitting in the input queue until that turn ends.

dsh-swarm-orchestrator README · Notices reach the running chat (0.6.32)：- The plugin reads the dispatching session's live status and picks the channel: **idle → one ordinary turn**, **busy → `steer`**, which the running turn consumes at its next step. A mid-turn `followup` is claimed only after the running turn fully ends, and a turn that ends by abort replays only a latched wake — production left a completed-run notice parked behind the dispatch turn until a human clicked **Steer**.
- A host without `steer` gets the no-wake `inject` fallback, and a host that cannot report status keeps `followup`, preserving legacy best-effort behavior. Missing sessions and delivery errors remain contained; delivery is not guaranteed.
- Notices are attributed as plugin **notices**, not user messages: they render as a collapsed `dsh-swarm-orchestrator` row with a one-line summary, and they are no longer mistaken for human authorization by goal, skill-scan or wake-budget policy. Their producer-owned source kind is `plugin:dsh-swarm-orchestrator`, matching migrated historical notices; the retired `{ kind: 'plugin', plugin: 'dsh-swarm-orchestrator' }` wrapper is rejected by native V4 session persistenc
dsh-swarm-orchestrator README · Hardening and Flow updates (0.6.31)：This release adds lifecycle, admission and persistence safeguards, plus a readable, left-aligned Flow view.

dsh-swarm-orchestrator README · Hardening and Flow updates (0.6.31)：- HTTP reads and actions share host admission checks; JSON and SSE have explicit resource bounds.
- Children inherit a captured sandbox ceiling with noninteractive approvals; command evidence uses the DSH Shell under that same authority, never an unrestricted host subprocess.
- Cancellation keeps capacity reserved until child/evidence cleanup actually finishes. A cleanup failure remains visible and retains its reservation.
- Attempt-bound reports are recovery hints, not approval: recovered work passes the same command-evidence and human/agent review gates as normal completion.
- Reviewer unavailability or exhausted retries are recorded separately from approval. Builder and reviewer identities, fallback models and actual effort pins remain distinct.
- Each owner receives only their own waits. The shared SSE transport fences stale responses; settings drafts survive progress and show observed conflicts. Saves are not server-side compare-and-swap.
- Flow waves, scheduler and report start at the same left edge. Nodes start at readable 100% size; use the zoom controls or **Fit** for a full-chart overview. The scaled foot
dsh-swarm-orchestrator README · Reliability notes (v0.5.8 – v0.6.17)：Diagnosed from 47 recorded runs / 184 task failures plus the incidents below, then fixed and regression-tested:

dsh-swarm-orchestrator README · Reliability notes (v0.5.8 – v0.6.17)：- **Evidence commands run under PowerShell** (bash elsewhere) from the workspace root, and the `evidence.commands` schema says so. Previously they were handed to `cmd.exe`, so a perfectly normal PowerShell gate (`if (Test-Path …) { exit 0 }`) failed the task — 32% of all recorded task failures. Commands are mandatory gates; `evidence.files` checks expected artifacts without a shell and produces advisory warnings, not a completion gate.
- **`modlens` is denied to swarm roles** by default in the shipped roster guidance: it is an interactive tool that asks the user a question, and swarm children run non-interactively. Add it back per-role from the Roster if your deployment has a headless vision provider.
- **A task report that does not claim `"status": "completed"` is never adopted** — adoption cannot mask unfinished work.
- **An adopted report must belong to the exact live attempt.** New reports use hashed run/attempt/task namespaces and carry matching identities; missing, wrong or revoked identities are rejected. Only legacy reports use the old task-id path and timestamp compatibility check. Adoption still runs evi

dsh-swarm-orchestrator README · The dashboard：- **Board** — runs on the left, task columns (Queued / Running / Done / Failed) front and center. Click a task for its full brief, model, attempt count, interim agent notes, reviewer feedback, and retry. Completed runs fold into a report with per-task summaries and fallback/retry/review stats.
- **Flow** — the task DAG as a living flow chart: the scheduler at the top, tasks fanned out into parallel waves (same wave = runs concurrently), dependency arrows turning green as blockers complete, reviewer and write-scope hints on each node, all converging into the run report. You can see at a glance what ran in parallel, what ran in sequence, and exactly how far the run has gotten.
- **Roster** — the duty-table editor: per-role model pickers fed by your live catalog, fallback-chain ordering, effort ladder, concurrency caps, per-role spawn timeouts, tool filters, personas, custom roles, and an override lock for "hands off my table". The pickers list only providers you have configured in DSH (with API keys) and follow changes automatically — DSH 0.1.6+ required.
- **Everywhere else** — a 🐝 status button in every session header, a small badge for

dsh-swarm-orchestrator README · How a run works：1. **Dispatch** — tell your agent what you want; it calls `swarm_dispatch` with a task graph. Runs start gated: *planning*, zero agents spawned.
2. **Execute** — the architect reviews the proposal and produces `PLAN.md`; then parallel builders start.
3. **Watch** — **Board** shows the kanban; **Flow** shows the workflow chart; click any task for its drawer.

dsh-swarm-orchestrator README · 1 · Install：From this GitHub repo (pnpm will run the package's `prepare` script to build from source):

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add github:linkbag/dsh-swarm-orchestrator
```

pnpm ≥ 10 asks you to allow that build first — add the exact key it prints to the profile's `pnpm-workspace.yaml`:

```yaml
allowBuilds:
  dsh-swarm-orchestrator: true
```

dsh-swarm-orchestrator README · 1 · Install：and re-run the `add`. (That allowance executes this package's code on your machine at install time — the usual trust rule applies; pin a commit if you prefer: `github:linkbag/dsh-swarm-orchestrator#<sha>`.)

Or install prebuilt from npm — no build allowance needed:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-swarm-orchestrator
```

dsh-swarm-orchestrator README · 1 · Install：Then restart `dsh web` (or reload the profile). You should see the **Swarm** tab next to Chat, a 🐝 button in every session header, and **Settings → AI Swarm** (the title shows the running version — a quick way to confirm the install).

dsh-swarm-orchestrator README · 2 · Assign models to roles：Open the **Swarm** tab in any chat and switch to **Roster** — or open **Settings → AI Swarm**, the same editor reachable from anywhere. The four built-in roles:

| Role | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **architect** | Reviews the proposal, refines it into `PLAN.md` |
| **builder** | Implements one task to completion, with verification |
| **reviewer** | Judges completed work against the task brief |
| **integrator** | Merges parallel work and ships the result |

dsh-swarm-orchestrator README · 2 · Assign models to roles：For each role, pick a model from the dropdown. It lists **every provider configured in DSH** (DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi, Claude, …), grouped by provider — the same live catalog as the Models settings page. Leave a role on **inherit deployment default** to use whatever model the dispatching chat runs on.

Optional, per role (all have sane defaults):

dsh-swarm-orchestrator README · 2 · Assign models to roles：- **Fallback chain** — models tried in order if the primary is unavailable.
- **Effort + effort ladder** — the role's pinned reasoning effort; rungs advance per attempt and always end unpinned, and a level a model's declared map excludes is stripped before spawning.
- **Concurrency cap** — limit simultaneous agents of this role.
- **Spawn timeout** — per-role override of the no-progress window that reclaims a silent child.
- **Tool filter** — deny specific tools to this role's agents (e.g. a read-only reviewer).
- **Persona** — the role's standing instructions.
dsh-swarm-orchestrator README · 2 · Assign models to roles：Missing a model? Add the provider in DSH **Settings → Models** first, then hit **refresh catalog** in the Roster.

dsh-swarm-orchestrator README · 3 · Dispatch your first swarm：In any chat, just ask:

> *"Spawn a swarm: audit every package.json in this repo for stale deps, one task per package, then an integrator compiles a summary table. Review the integrator's output."*

or the one-shot form:

```text
/swarm build a landing page for this project
```

Your agent will call `swarm_dispatch` with a task DAG. (It may plan first itself — that's fine: an architect agent reviews and refines whatever plan it sends.)

dsh-swarm-orchestrator README · 4 · Watch the run：- **Board** shows the kanban; **Flow** shows the same run as a workflow chart (scheduler → parallel waves → report); click any task for its drawer — brief, model, interim notes, reviewer feedback, retry.
- Tasks with `reviewGate: "human"` park on the board for your Approve/Reject.
- The dispatching chat gets a live progress card; the 🐝 header button and the bottom-right badge track active runs from anywhere.

dsh-swarm-orchestrator README · 5 · Read the report：When the run finishes it folds into a report: per-task summaries, models used, fallback/retry/review stats. The whole history is an append-only event log you can replay.

> **Defaults worth knowing:** every run starts with an architect review of the plan (skip per dispatch with `architectReview: false`); dispatching into a workspace that already has an active run raises a warning — parallel workstreams belong in one DAG; the roster, badge, and header button are global across workspaces.

dsh-swarm-orchestrator README · Talking to it：Everything is driven from normal chat — no config files to hand-edit:

> *"Spawn a swarm: audit every package.json in this repo for stale deps, one task per package, then an integrator compiles a summary table. Review the integrator's output."*

or the one-shot form: `/swarm build a landing page for this project` (plans it, then executes it).

dsh-swarm-orchestrator README · Talking to it：| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `swarm_dispatch` | Submit a run: title, objective, task DAG (id / subject / description / role / blockedBy / reviewBy / reviewGate / model / evidence / writes). |
| `swarm_status` | The board in text: runs, task states, models in use, latest notes. |
| `swarm_wait` | Wait on meaningful changes with a durable cursor, terminal/drained modes and bounded text; optional all-event mode. |
| `swarm_retry` | Requeue a failed/blocked/held task using its observed identity after fixing the cause (dispatching session only). |
| `swarm_interrupt` | Abort a stalled/running task and requeue it in the same run — no relief sibling needed (dispatching session only). |
| `swarm_complete` | Mark a task completed when its work was finished outside the swarm (dispatching session only) — keeps the run record in sync with reality. |
| `swarm_report` | Task agents post interim notes to the board (authenticated to their own task). |

dsh-swarm-orchestrator README · Talking to it：Tasks also accept an **evidence contract** — `evidence: { files: [...], commands: [...], artifacts: [...] }` — whose file/structural enforcement follows the explicit policy above; an **advisory write scope** — `writes: [files]` — that warns about overlap but does not lock or intercept writes; and a **human review gate** that parks the verdict on the dashboard. A failing evidence command no longer re-runs the finished work: it gets one command-only recheck, and if the command still fails — non-zero exit or timeout (`evidenceTimeoutMs`, default 120 s) — the task parks on the board for a human verdict, with the exit code and an output tail recorded in the event log.

dsh-swarm-orchestrator README · Configuration：Everything has a default; override in your profile's `cordis.patch.yml`:

```yaml
- id: swarm
  require: dsh-swarm-orchestrator
  config:
    storageDir: !!js dshHomePath("storages/swarm")   # event log + duty table

dsh-swarm-orchestrator README · Runtime control：The runtime parameters listed below are **tunable from the dashboard**; the new `maxAttemptSeconds` ceiling is a profile configuration value, not a dashboard override. Those runtime updates need no YAML editing or restart. Open **Settings → AI Swarm → Runtime tuning** (or the **Roster tab → Runtime tuning**) and adjust:

dsh-swarm-orchestrator README · Runtime control：| Parameter | Default | What it controls |
|---|---|---|
| Max concurrent agents | 50 | Simultaneously running task agents **per run** |
| Global agent cap | 100 | Max agents across **all** runs — concurrent runs share this budget (60+40, not 100+100). These agents run in-process and share the host Node heap: the high default suits a large machine, so lower it on a constrained one |
| Spawn stagger (ms) | 750 | Delay between launches in one wave — softens simultaneous provider load |
| Retry backoff base (ms) | 5000 | Failed tasks wait base × 2^attempt before retrying (5s → 10s → 20s) — prevents synchronized retry cascades when a provider outage kills all tasks at once |
| Circuit breaker threshold | 3 | Failures within 30 seconds before pausing all retries (0 = off) — detects provider-wide outages |
| Circuit breaker cooldown (ms) | 60000 | How long retries pause after the breaker trips |
| Nudge after silence (min) | 20 | Board marker for silent tasks — 0 = off |
| Stale timeout (sec) | 14400 | Last-resort reclaim for agents that go completely silent (4 hours) |
| Spawn timeout (sec) | 3600 | Heartbeat-renewed liveness window per ch

dsh-swarm-orchestrator README · Runtime control：Changes are **applied immediately** (no restart) and **persisted to `runtime.json`** in the swarm storage directory, overriding the profile's `cordis.patch.yml` values. They survive host restarts.

> 💡 If you run multiple swarms from different workspaces in parallel, watch the global agent cap (default 100 in-process agents) and keep to max 2 concurrent runs. If you experience `ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED` (host crash), lower the global cap in the Runtime settings.

dsh-swarm-orchestrator README · Under the hood：- **Host half** (Node): a `SwarmService` — duty-table store, append-only JSONL event store, projection fold, the dispatcher (parallel one-shot subagents behind a service-owned anchor agent), review loop, watchdog, pause/resume, and `/swarm/*` HTTP + SSE routes.
- **Client half** (browser): the Swarm tab, the chat progress card, the header popover, and the Settings section — all fed by board snapshots over a single reference-counted SSE connection. Model pickers use the same LLM RPCs as the Models settings page.
- **Per-role reasoning effort** is supplied in initial child options before the first request, then maintained by an ownership-fenced `agent/request` waterfall. Validation is provider-qualified for every actual candidate/rung, and build/review metadata records actual starts separately.
- **Deterministic replay**: state is a fold over the event log, with legality guards — a hostile or duplicated event stream cannot resurrect an aborted run or complete a task twice.
dsh-swarm-orchestrator README · Known limits：Written plainly, because a limit you discover in production costs far more than one you read here.

dsh-swarm-orchestrator README · Known limits：- **The board reports disk truth, and the disk can lag the model.** A task agent may finish its work without performing every bookkeeping step the protocol asks of it (for example, writing its `.dsh-swarm/task-<id>.json` report). The board shows what was actually recorded, not what the agent claimed. Treat a task's summary as evidence of what was recorded, and verify deliverables yourself.
- **Evidence contracts are advisory for files, hard for commands.** On advisory/legacy runs, a missing or empty `evidence.files` entry becomes a board warning; new `evidence: "required"` policy holds invalid files/structural artifacts, while a failing `evidence.commands` entry always blocks completion (after one command-only recheck, a persistent failure parks the task for a human rather than re-running the work). Scope control is therefore a completion-time audit, not write interception — nothing stops an agent from writing outside its declared `writes` scope; the dispatcher only warns about overlapping scopes at dispatch time.

dsh-swarm-orchestrator README · Status：**0.6.33 implements the reviewed hardening plan (S0–S7); 0.6.32's status-aware notices and 0.6.31's lifecycle hardening and readable Flow remain.** Type checking, the host/client build, the content receipt/compiled-export verification, and the offline suite pass — **1,005 tests across 38 files** — covering dispatch, authority, admission, persistence, lifecycle, recovery, routing, review gates, notifications, transport, settings and client rendering, plus the new policy/artifact, replay, ownership, ledger and coordination suites. Tests use fake subagents and owned temporary storage; deployment suites are excluded unless explicit fixtures are exported. Historical headless Chrome Flow checks are not validation of this release against the operator's authenticated GUI. No host reload, frozen research rerun, clinical admission or production mutation is claimed.
